The hut was smaller than they had imagined. Its door was bolted from the outside, and the shutters rattled in the wind. They forced the bolt open and carried their packs inside, where a stone stove waited in the corner. That night the storm shook the walls for hours. Nobody slept well. By morning the world outside was white and silent, and the trail they had climbed the day before had vanished completely. They melted snow for tea and counted the supplies twice. The guide said the weather would break by evening, and he was right. The clouds parted at dusk, and a red glow spread across the peaks. They stood outside the hut and watched the light fade, saying nothing, because there was nothing that needed to be said.
